n7afd28abc553: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence and digital technologies is generating unprecedented e-waste streams rich in secondary gold resources, yet sustainable recovery strategies remain scarce. Here, we report a bioderived, environmentally degradable metal–organic framework (MOF)/oligomer composite (SU-102/pGSH) constructed via host–guest self-assembly of glutathione (GSH) within a Zr-ellagate framework. The composite integrates abundant electron-rich functional groups into a robust porous architecture, achieving a remarkable gold uptake capacity of 4385 mg·g–1, the highest reported for MOF-based adsorbents. It also exhibits outstanding selectivity in complex e-waste leachates. Mechanistic investigations reveal synergistic coordination with abundant electron-rich groups, followed by electron-transfer reduction of Au(III) to Au(0). Importantly, the spent adsorbent could degrade into benign mineral phases and natural metabolites with negligible phytotoxicity, ensuring a safe end-of-life pathway. Preliminary techno-economic analysis indicates favorable economic potential for practical implementation. By integrating efficient gold recovery with sustainable material design and end-of-life management, this work provides a viable strategy for circular water treatment.
ndbe06309ac39: A strategy to switch the chirality of spin texture in hybrid perovskites, without the aid of an applied electric field, has been established. The switching of spin texture chirality can be used to manipulate the spin-to-charge conversion. The electric current, generated by coherent magnon mediated spin current or photo induced spin current, changes sign during the transition from static to dynamic Rashba effect, which demonstrates its applications in spintronic and magnonic devices.
n89865298f348: Nanostructured gold thin films are widely used biosensing materials due to their inertness, high surface area, favorable electrochemical properties, antifouling abilities, and biocompatibility. However, the structural integrity of thin films is easily compromised when stretched. Here we present a liquid metal synthesis route that allows room temperature fabrication of nanoscale thickness, nanoporous gold (NPAu) electrodes on stretchable polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS). Carbon nanofibers (CNFs) are introduced to maintain electrical conductivity of NPAu by suppressing crack formation/propagation and establishing intercrack conductive pathways. The PDMS-supported, CNF-reinforced NPAu retains its electrical conductivity at strains up to 80% and a relative resistance change of 11% under 2000 cyclic loads at 20% strain, demonstrating exceptional stability. NPAu-CNF demonstrates an electroactive surface area 1.8 times that of commercial Au electrodes, along with superior antifouling performance. These findings establish a protocol for realizing stretchability in thin film bioelectrodes, meeting the demand for developing conformable yet highly integrated biosensors.
n5557e17b7c3b: Polarons, formed by coupling electrons with lattice vibrations, are of intense interest in topological semimetals owing to their crucial role in dictating high-speed topological optoelectronics. However, polarons in topological semimetals have thus far been exclusively observed as light-induced transient quasiparticles, leaving equilibrium polarons and their ultrafast dynamics elusive. Here, using time-resolved magneto-terahertz spectroscopy, we demonstrate the ultrafast optical undressing of polarons in a Cd3As2 thin film. In equilibrium, a magnetic-field-induced spectral splitting near the 1.22-terahertz phonon mode reveals an 87% enhancement of the carrier effective mass due to the polaron effect. Upon photoexcitation, the enhanced carrier effective mass collapses within 5 ps, reflecting the transient undressing of this pre-existing polaronic state. Notably, this anomalous suppression contrasts sharply with prior studies where optical excitation exclusively triggers polaron formation in topological semimetals. This study provides deep insights into the ultrafast magneto-optical dynamics of pre-existing polarons, advancing the design of high-performance topological devices.
nf038001032e3: Metal/topological insulator van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures offer a platform for engineering emergent quantum states beyond isolated layers. While proximity effects in covalently bonded systems are well studied, coupling depth across vdW interfaces remains unclear. Using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy and first-principles calculations, we investigate the thickness dependence of TiTe2/Bi2Te3 electronic states. Despite nominally weak vdW bonding, the buried interface induces emergent bands and splitting near a band crossing, consistent with hybridization. Interface-induced features persist in the bilayer, while band evolution nearly saturates in thicker films. Even at four layers, the electronic structure does not simply recover to the intrinsic TiTe2 limit, consistent with finite-depth coupling that substantially reshapes the overlayer bands. Charge redistribution and a moiré-modulated interfacial potential contribute to this reconstruction. Finite-depth coupling may be a hallmark of strongly coupled vdW heterostructures and guide topological and quantum electronic device design.
naee7d83563d4: Room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) materials are promising for information encryption and anticounterfeiting. However, realizing long-wavelength RTP of carbon dots (CDs) is challenging owing to unstable triplet states and strong nonradiative decay. Herein, we construct a hydrogen-bonded organic framework (HOF) through molecular self-assembly and realize the in situ generation of CDs within the HOF matrix. By further incorporating Rhodamine B (RhB) into the HOF, a donor–acceptor resonance energy transfer (RET) system is established, enabling efficient red RTP emission. In this system, the HOF matrix provides a confined environment for the CDs and RhB. Meanwhile, the hydrogen-bonded network restricts excited-state molecular motions and suppresses nonradiative relaxation. The optimized CDs-RhB@HOF composite exhibits outstanding red phosphorescence centered at 600 nm, achieving a high PLQY of 34.20% (versus 0.71% for CDs@HOF) and a prolonged lifetime of 458 ms. The composite material has been successfully applied to multilevel anticounterfeiting encryption.
nc617f0bb268d: Natural structural colors often emerge from interactions between chiral lattices and three-dimensional (3D) microstructures, yet integrating surface topography with structural order in artificial photonic materials remains challenging. Here, we develop a light-driven self-growth strategy for programmable 3D photonic structures by engineering through-thickness gradients in a preassembled chiral nematic cellulose scaffold. Confined UV photopolymerization drives localized reactions and directional mass transport, creating coupled gradients in cross-linking density, polymer concentration, and helical pitch. These gradients enable continuous structural-color tuning from blue to red, while differential swelling-induced buckling produces patterned protrusions with programmable heights. The resulting interpenetrating network provides structural integrity and mechanical robustness. Combined with photomask lithography, this approach yields spatially resolved multicolor architectures featuring programmable 3D topographies, angle-dependent optical responses, and self-cleaning properties. It further enables four-channel optical encryption integrating polarization, multipeak reflection, 3D topography, and photoluminescence, demonstrating gradient engineering as a versatile route to advanced multifunctional bioinspired photonic material design.
nfd14b2f45798: Efficient lithium recovery from salt-lake brines is vital for lithium-resource supply. Nevertheless, practical application of titanium-based H2TiO3 (HTO) ion sieves is limited by insufficient adsorption performance. Herein, a high-performance HTO adsorbent (HTO-VMT) was fabricated using vermiculite to regulate the spatial coordination environment and surface hydrophilicity of HTO. Theoretical calculations and experimental analysis reveal that vermiculite, as a Si source and support for HTO, enables interfacial Si migration through isovalent substitution of Ti atoms, leading to atomic-level integration into the HTO crystal lattice. The Si substitution results in an upward shift of the p-band center of O of HTO, which enhanced hybridizations between Li 2s and O 2p orbitals, thus accelerating lithium adsorption rates in the surface diffusion phase. Thanks to an optimal coordination structure and surface hydrophilicity, HTO-VMT exhibits exceptional lithium extraction performance, surpassing state-of-the-art counterparts. This work provides design insights for Li-selective adsorbents via mineral-mediated atomic-scale coordination modulation.
n98307b90e942: We report a nonlinear Hall effect in a high-mobility InAs quantum-well two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) with coexisting Rashba and Dresselhaus spin–orbit interactions. Under zero magnetic field, a second-harmonic transverse electric field emerges that scales quadratically with current density and is significantly larger than the second-harmonic longitudinal response. Angle-dependent measurements reveal a pronounced 2-fold anisotropy that follows the combined spin–orbit field. This 2-fold symmetry reflects the anisotropic spin–orbit field generated by coexisting Rashba and Dresselhaus interactions rather than crystal symmetry. The normalized signal reaches ∼10–9 V–1 m and persists up to room temperature. Conductivity scaling shows a quadratic dependence consistent with skew-scattering-dominated transport. These results establish conventional semiconductor 2DEGs as a promising platform for spin-orbit-driven nonlinear transport and rectification functionalities.
na3770c56b45a: Dynamic restructuring of metal nanocrystals (MNCs) in reactive gas atmospheres challenges the static paradigm of shape-controlled model catalysis. Quantifying their structural lifetimes under operating conditions is essential, yet predicting atomistic kinetics over macroscopic time scales remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we transform unpredictable structural lifetimes into a manageable variable using an improved environmental kinetic Monte Carlo (iEKMC) method. It overcomes traditional time scale limits and predicts Pt NC reshaping kinetics across macroscopic time domains under CO atmospheres. By resolving the combined effects of initial morphology, particle size, and temperature, we establish a quantitative framework that determines the reshaping time of MNCs under reaction conditions, showing consistency with benchmarking experiments. We demonstrate that selected combinations of particle size and reaction conditions can effectively mitigate restructuring, preserving predesigned MNC morphologies over day-scale observation windows. This work evaluates and manages operando shape stability in a predictive strategy, restoring the core validity of shape-controlled model catalysis.
n23d6cb0780ae: Superconductivity above the liquid-nitrogen temperature remains rare in two-dimensional elemental crystals, where strong covalent bonding often yields high phonon frequencies but insufficient electron–phonon coupling. Here, using first-principles calculations and fully anisotropic Migdal–Eliashberg theory, we predict tetralayer kagome borophene (TKB) stabilized by ABAB covalent stacking, as a liquid-nitrogen-temperature elemental superconductor. With a predicted critical temperature of ∼100–113 K, TKB sets a record-high value among previously reported elemental superconductors. Unlike known high-Tc boron-based superconductors dominated by in-plane σ-bonding states and high-frequency in-plane B–B stretching modes, TKB realizes an out-of-plane s–pz-bonding-mediated pairing mechanism, in which interlayer s–pz bonding states at the Fermi level are strongly coupled to low-frequency out-of-plane vibrations of boron atoms. These results reveal a distinct out-of-plane pairing channel in multilayer borophene and establish covalent stacking engineering as a potential route for high-Tc superconductivity in two-dimensional materials.
n03432ac94267: Characterizing multiphoton emission is essential for understanding and developing quantum light sources. Emerging single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) array detectors offer new opportunities but require tailored analysis strategies. Here we present such approaches for colloidal nanoparticles with long-lived multiexciton states, where multiple bright excitonic and charged states contribute to emission. Using CdS/CdSe/CdS quantum shells as a model system, we combine high-throughput characterization across more than 1000 particles with state-resolved spectroscopy. Double projection of the sample image onto the detector prevents crosstalk artifacts and improves data quality. High-throughput photon-correlation measurements on a frame-based SPAD-array camera quantify biexciton emission efficiency and reveal particle-to-particle variations. Reference time-gated measurements distinguish individual particles from clusters. An event-based linear SPAD array resolves bimodal biexciton spectra but reveals no strong blue shift relative to the exciton, in contrast to previous reports. Our study presents insights into multiphoton emission by colloidal quantum shells and experimental strategies for quantum-emitter characterization.
n70e4fe37bfcc: Organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) have emerged as promising platforms for bioelectronics and neuromorphic devices because of their unique ionic–electronic coupling. The key to unlocking high-performance operations lies in achieving rapid and efficient bulk doping, yet this remains critically hampered by limited ion accessibility, particularly within the hydrophobic bulk of organic mixed ionic–electronic conductors (OMIECs). This mini-review highlights recent molecular and processing engineering strategies to enhance ion penetration and ion–electron coupling in OECT channels. Molecular-level tuning, such as side-chain and backbone modulation, in addition to processing approaches, including the use of additives, dopants, cross-linked networks, solvent engineering, patterned transport architectures, and interface microstructure control, are discussed. Throughout, we place special emphasis on elucidating the complex relationships between molecular structure, processing-derived morphology, interfacial environments, and ion–transport dynamics, complemented by advanced characterization approaches that probe ion transport and its coupling with hydration and structural evolution. This holistic understanding is pivotal for rational performance optimization. Finally, we highlight emerging frontiers in advanced characterization, multiscale simulation, and data-driven design, which are expected to expedite the discovery of high-performance OMIECs and OECTs with balanced and enhanced mixed transport properties.
n6f0474f86028: Zirconium catalysis has remained largely confined to Lewis acid and redox chemistry, with only isolated examples of photocatalytic C–H activation. Now trifunctional zirconium catalysis enables modular benzylamine synthesis from alkanes, aldehydes and nitriles by integrating photochemical, redox and Lewis acid reactivity.
nd2fb861fb755: Electrochemical kinetics are shaped by both the thermodynamic driving force and interfacial polarization. Now it has been shown that that activation energies decrease with increasing potential but increase with greater deviation of the potential from the potential of zero total charge, revealing a multidimensional kinetic landscape.
n501fcdefddd6: Applied potential controls charge-transfer kinetics, but thermochemical steps can limit electrocatalytic rates. Now it has been shown that CO-to-methanol conversion shifts from charge-transfer-limited kinetics to adsorption-limited kinetics as overpotential increases, establishing CO adsorption energy as a descriptor of the thermochemical constraint.
nbeeb6fe1da3e: Anode-free sodium batteries eliminate excessive sodium on the anode, maximizing cell-level energy density, but are limited by irreversible sodium loss during electroplating–stripping. Now, a low-strain cyclic solvent forms an oligomerized interphase, enabling highly reversible sodium deposition without functional additives or electrode modifications.
n1ea9da55a0c2: Formamidinium (FA)-doped caesium lead triiodide, Cs(FA)PbI3, is a promising front-cell absorber for tandem solar cells owing to its good stability, yet obtaining high-quality films remains a challenge. Here we identify that sparse doping of oversized FA cations induces severe grain boundary (GB) distortion, thereby facilitating defect generation and performance deterioration. To mitigate this, we develop a Pb-based metallomesogen that forms a mesophase exhibiting both solid-like and liquid-like properties. The phase characteristics enable the Pb-based metallomesogen to distribute uniformly along GBs of Cs(FA)PbI3 film, alleviating GB distortion, relieving shear strain, preserving lattice integrity and mitigating defect formation. Consequently, perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells based on a 1.66-eV Cs(FA)PbI3 absorber incorporating a Br-containing GB modifier achieve a champion efficiency of 32.08% (certified 31.62%), retaining 95% of the initial performance after ~3,000 h under maximum power point tracking and 93% after 1,500 h under 85% relative humidity and 85 °C damp-heat stressing. Formamidinium–caesium lead triiodide perovskites show promise in terms of stability, yet their solar cell efficiency remains limited. Li et al. use a metallomesogen with mesophase to stabilize perovskite grain boundaries, improving both the efficiency and stability of perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells.
nda107e17f06c: Anode-free sodium batteries are limited by irreversible sodium loss during cycling. Here the authors introduce a moderate-strain cyclic ether that redirects electrolyte decomposition to form a thin, robust interphase, thereby minimizing sodium consumption and extending cycling stability.
n93323abf382c: The deformation of flexible ligands in polymer-grafted nanoparticles enables initially isotropic particles to produce effective valency, accessing lattice symmetries with unexpected deviations from densest packing or highest coordination number.
ndf110d2ff713: Laser-based additive manufacturing enables the formation of a self-assembled precipitate cellular network in a multi-principal element alloy, which sustains a yield strength above 1 GPa and a uniform elongation of approximately 20% over a wide temperature range.
nc1912749a4a1: Non-resonant excitation of WS2 in-plane microcavities generates waveguide exciton–polaritons that carry spin-polarized currents over distances exceeding 90 μm at room temperature and reveal a non-resonantly pumped optical spin Hall effect.
n1dc2d1788181: Atomically thin amorphous materials combine atomic-scale thickness with local structural disorder, creating unusual transport, interfacial, electronic and catalytic properties. This Review outlines the mechanism-guided synthesis of atomically thin amorphous materials, scalable manufacturing and structure–property relationships and discusses AI-assisted closed-loop strategies for application-oriented design and wafer-scale production.
n41d3f727dd7e: High‐entropy oxides (HEOs) with photothermal conversion capability provide a promising platform for enhancing the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in electrocatalytic water splitting. In this work, the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM), the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM), and photothermal effects are integrated into a single reaction system through Fe doping into HEOs. By combining theoretical calculations and experimental characterizations, we reveal that Fe doping optimally tailors the adsorption/desorption energetics of intermediates along the AEM, while simultaneously introducing oxygen vacancies that modulate the metal‐oxygen electronic environment and promote LOM participation. This dual‐pathway activation, enabled by the high‐entropy rock‐salt structure, enhances catalytic activity. In addition, the photothermal effect of (FeMgCoNiCuZn)O1−x can accelerate interfacial charge‐transfer kinetics and facilitate OOH* deprotonation. Under Xe‐lamp irradiation, Fe doping lowers the apparent activation energy for OER from 15.3 to 11.2 kJ mol−1, and the catalyst achieves oxygen evolution current densities of 10 and 50 mA cm−2 at overpotentials of 159 and 247 mV. More importantly, it exhibits outstanding long‐term durability, maintaining stable operation for over 1500 h at 1 A cm−2. These findings underscore the potential of Fe‐doping hexanary HEOs as a highly efficient candidate for electrocatalytic water splitting.
n0a01d6d9ef0e: Controlling lattice‐oxygen reactivity in transition‐metal (TM) oxides is essential for Mars‐van Krevelen selective oxidations, yet conventional strategies that tune TM1‐O‐TM2 bridges suffer from covalent competition between adjacent redox‐active cations, which generates site heterogeneity and degrades selectivity. Herein, taking Ruddlesden–Popper LaSrFeO4 (A2BO4) as a model, we demonstrate that constructing asymmetric A‐O‐B motifs (i.e., La‐O‐Fe and Sr‐O‐Fe) provides a distinct route to overcome this limitation. Combined experiments and DFT calculations reveal that the A‐O‐B configuration could convert redox‐inert A‐site cations into direct electronic contributors to oxygen, which unlocks the covalent competition, substantially enabling promoted electron density over oxygen and enhanced Fe─O bond covalency. Consequently, LaSrFeO4 displays much lower methane activation barrier (∼1.24 eV) than its perovskite counterpart, LaFeO3, with an Fe‐O‐Fe motif (1.90 eV), ultimately affording a 2.35‐fold increase in syngas yield with 97% selectivity. This discovery reveals that asymmetric A‐O‐B coordination may serve as a promising structural strategy, distinct from B‐O‐B modulation, for modulating the electronic properties and reactivity of lattice oxygen.
n938221ff7e80: Detecting single molecules with high sensitivity and specificity is of great scientific and practical interest. Surface‐enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) is an ultrasensitive molecular detection technique for single‐molecule detection. However, the fabrication of ultrasensitive single‐molecule SERS substrates remains a key goal. Herein, we report an acoustic levitation assisted containerless strategy to construct InSe‐Au Schottky junctions with robust interfacial bonding, achieving single‐molecule detection of zeptomolar level and an EF of 1010. The controllable acoustic radiation pressure inside the levitated droplet induced robust interfacial coupling of InSe‐Au Schottky junctions, which was verified by HAADF‐STEM etc. The bianalyte Poisson‐binomial statistical model confirmed single molecule origin of Raman signals. Linear relationship between detection probability and ultralow Rhodamine B (RhB) concentration was established. Single molecule SERS mapping directly visualized molecular adsorption sites, identifying strongly bonded junction interface as critical signal enhancement region. The enhancement mechanism is primarily attributed to chemical enhancement, wherein the built‐in electric field facilitates multiple photoinduced charge‐transfer pathways, while the localized surface plasmon resonance of Au couples with out‐of‐plane dipole of InSe to enhance light harvesting. This strategy is material‐generalizable, as demonstrated by WSe2/GaSe‐Au systems with attomolar limits. This work provides new insights into engineering strongly bonded heterojunctions for single‐molecule sensing devices.
n98f2b67dc41f: The performance of Cu2ZnSn(SxSe1−x)4 (CZTSSe) solar cells is primarily limited by an inability to control the selenization process, where non-uniform selenium distribution leads to profound Cu–Zn cation disorder and associated performance losses. Compositional engineering, such as in (AgxCu1−x)2ZnSn(SxSe1−x)4 (ACZTSSe), can mitigate some defects; however, it fails to address the root cause: mastering the reaction kinetics to achieve elemental homogeneity. Herein, we introduce a self-sacrificing Ag2Se layer on Mo substrates that enables a bottom-up, cooperative Ag–Se diffusion pathway during grain growth. The rapid migration of Ag atoms modifies the local chemical environment, thereby acting as a kinetic driver that dramatically enhances the selenium diffusion flux. Molecular dynamics simulations confirm a 28.6% increase in the selenium diffusion coefficient (D Se), demonstrating that this kinetic enhancement activates the cooperative Ag–Se diffusion mechanism, thereby achieving a macroscopic improvement in material homogeneity. The resultant absorber exhibits an unprecedented, near-linear elemental distribution, which effectively suppresses Cu-related antisite defects (e.g., CuZn and CuSn). This superior homogeneity minimizes bulk recombination and facilitates efficient carrier transport, thereby providing a fundamental basis for the enhancement of photoelectric properties. Consequently, the champion device treated with 65 nm Ag2Se (ASe 65) achieves a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 14.36% (certified as 13.91%), primarily due to a remarkable enhancement in short-circuit current density (J sc) and fill factor (FF). This work not only provides a foundational understanding of cooperative diffusion chemistry, but also establishes a novel paradigm for manipulating reaction kinetics in solid-state energy materials.
n7d674c016612: Ni‐rich layered oxide cathodes with high energy density are regarded as one of the most promising cathode candidates for achieving next‐generation high‐energy lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs). However, increasing the Ni content introduces critical challenges, including undesirable phase transitions, sluggish Li+ transport, and intergranular cracking, which hinder their large‐scale application. This work demonstrates an Al3+/Ta5+ co‐doping strategy, enabling homogeneous Li+ transport in a Ni‐rich cathode by forming LiNi0.94Ta0.01Al0.05O2 (LNTAO) with refined grains and suppressed Li/Ni cation mixing. The achieved homogenization suppresses high‐voltage phase transitions and facilitates Li+ intercalation/deintercalation during cycling. It also preserves the Ni valence state and Ni─O coordination environment, maintains grain‐boundary integrity, and suppresses interfacial side reactions during prolonged cycling. Enabled by these advantages, the cycle and rate performance of the Ni‐rich cathode are effectively enhanced. This Al3+/Ta5+ co‐doping strategy provides fundamental materials‐design insights into enhancing the electrochemical performance of Ni‐rich layered cathodes through the homogenization of Li+ transport.
nc504ec95a05e: The role of copper in Bi2Te3-based thermoelectric materials is not well understood, and there are conflicting results regarding its impact on thermoelectric properties. Some reports claim Cu is an electron donor after intercalating into the van der Waals-like gap of (Bi,Sb)2Te3, while others show it acting as an acceptor. Here, we help clarify this discrepancy experimentally and theoretically by demonstrating that Cu behaves as an amphoteric dopant (acceptor or donor) governed by its processing pathway. While kinetic pathways allow for Cu intercalation into the van der Waals-like gaps and electron donor behavior, thermodynamic equilibrium favors the substitution of Cu for Bi or Sb cations and acceptor behavior, which provides stronger chemical bonding and stability compared to intercalated Cu. When prioritizing thermodynamic stability, p-type Cu x Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3 exhibits high near-room-temperature zT values, with the best-performing composition among the investigated series reaching zT ≈1.36 ± 0.06 for four independently prepared x = 0.0025 samples. This arises from simultaneous improvements in both electronic properties (weighted mobility) and thermal properties (lattice thermal conductivity). Such improvements in zT for p-type (Bi,Sb)2Te3 in consistently manufactured materials would greatly benefit many applications for solid-state Peltier coolers and thermoelectric generators.
ndc9fbe7deb8f: Efficient xenon separation is important for noble‐gas management in liquid fluoride thorium reactor (LFTR) off‐gas systems. Here, JUC‐86, an ultramicroporous Ni‐based metal‐organic framework, is investigated for Xe‐selective capture and Ar/Kr/Xe separation. JUC‐86 features a crystallographic aperture of approximately 5.2 Å and model‐derived pore widths of 4.1‐5.2 Å. At 298 K and 1 bar, the adsorption capacities of Xe, Kr, and Ar reach 75.6, 57.2, and 17.3 cm3 g−1, respectively. IAST calculations, isosteric heats of adsorption, and host–guest calculations consistently indicate a stronger affinity toward Xe. Under continuous‐flow conditions, JUC‐86 exhibits reproducible Xe/Kr breakthrough separation, with an average Xe capture capacity of 1.41 mmol g−1 and Kr productivity above 99.9% purity. The material also captures trace Xe from dilute Xe/Kr/Ar streams and enables effective preparative chromatographic separation of Ar, Kr, and Xe over varied operating conditions. Bonding‐based analysis further suggests a meaningful degree of intrinsic γ‐radiation tolerance. These results demonstrate the potential of JUC‐86 for Xe‐selective capture and chromatographic noble‐gas separation in advanced nuclear off‐gas management.
n5ec9867d0541: Addiction‐related memories are associated with dysregulated neurotrophic signaling and maladaptive synaptic plasticity. However, it still remains challenging in translating such disease‐relevant molecular regulation into history‐dependent and programmable material states. Herein, a brain‐derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF)‐regulated ion–electronic memristive biointerface is developed by integrating a recognition module comprising a BDNF‐responsive aptamer and a tropomyosin receptor kinase B Fc chimera (TrkB‐Fc) with a photoactive sodium alginate (SA)/WO3 composite. Under 365 nm illumination, BDNF‐dependent interfacial regulation produces concentration‐ and history‐dependent conductance dynamics associated with W6+/W5+ mixed‐valence evolution. The device exhibits synaptic‐like responses, including paired‐pulse facilitation, learning–forgetting–relearning‐like dynamics, and reversible potentiation/depression‐like conductance modulation. These device‐state changes show functional correspondence with BDNF‐enhanced ΔFosB expression and morphine‐conditioned place preference, whereas ANA‐12 attenuates device‐state persistence and behavioral reinstatement in the respective experiments. Experimentally measured volatile responses are further used to construct reservoir states, while experimentally characterized nonvolatile conductance states provide a device‐informed basis for differential‐conductance readout‐weight representation in a software‐executed classification workflow, achieving a held‐out Fashion‐MNIST accuracy of 93.9%. Therefore, this work establishes a molecular‐to‐material transduction framework that converts neurotrophic regulation into programmable ion–electronic states and links biomolecular recognition, adaptive material dynamics, addiction‐related neuroplasticity, and proof‐of‐concept neuromorphic information processing.
nc07eee007534: The quality of the back contact critically determines the hole extraction efficiency and interfacial recombination losses in Sb2(S,Se)3 thin‐film solar cells. High‐efficiency devices typically use the Spiro‐OMeTAD/Au structure, but the reliance on Au electrodes increases material cost, creating an efficiency‐cost trade‐off. Here, we develop a cost‐effective Spiro‐OMeTAD/MoO3/Ag composite back contact that enables the use of a low‐cost electrode while maintaining efficient carrier extraction. The Spiro‐OMeTAD/MoO3/Ag composite back contact establishes a more favorable rear‐contact configuration, facilitating hole transfer while reducing carrier accumulation and interfacial recombination. Mild annealing further improves the back‐contact properties. Transient absorption spectroscopy (TAS), electrical, and photovoltaic measurements are interpreted together and consistently support improved interfacial carrier transfer with suppressed detrimental recombination. The optimized device achieves a PCE of 10.0%, approaching the performance level of reported Au‐based Sb2(S,Se)3 cells while using a low‐cost Ag‐based electrode. This work demonstrates an effective, economical back‐contact engineering strategy that delivers high performance with cost‐effectiveness.
ncc9f333c7e0e: Matching the mechanical properties of repair materials to tissue-specific demands remains a major challenge in soft-tissue repair. Here we report bioinspired anisotropic gelatin hydrogels formed by directional freezing and mechanically programmed through subsequent ionic treatment. By regulating intermolecular interactions while preserving the aligned, hierarchical porous architecture, this approach spans stiffnesses relevant to brain, kidney, tendon, and cartilage. Ion identity and treatment duration enable coordinated tuning of Young's modulus from 9.7 kPa to 3.59 MPa and tensile strength from 6 kPa to 14.25 MPa, together with broad regulation of viscoelasticity, extensibility, and fracture resistance. Multiscale SAXS/WAXS characterization, molecular simulations, and finite-element analysis reveal that ion-regulated chain association and hierarchical anisotropic organization collectively govern directional load transfer and mechanical reinforcement. Sodium citrate-treated AGE-SC 36H reaches a Young's modulus of 3.59 MPa, a tensile strength of 14.25 MPa, and a fracture energy of 413,305 J m− 2, while subsequent microbial transglutaminase (MTG) stabilization improves cyclic mechanical retention and resistance to swelling and enzymatic degradation under aqueous conditions. In a rat Achilles tendon model, AGE-SC 36H (MTG) promotes organized collagen remodeling and improves functional recovery over surgical repair alone. Overall, ionic regulation offers a general strategy for programming anisotropic hydrogel mechanics across material classes.
ndc73cb0edded: Electrochemical nitrate reduction reaction to ammonia (NO3RR) represents a sustainable pathway for closing the nitrogen cycle. However, the inherent activity-selectivity dilemma and fierce competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) severely restrict the practical application of noble-metal-based catalysts. Here, we report a universal low-temperature surface oxidation engineering strategy to reconstruct noble-metal (Ru, Ir, Pd, Pt) electrocatalysts. The resulting modification achieves simultaneous enhancement of NO3RR activity and efficient HER suppression, addressing a key challenge that is difficult to balance in conventional noble-metal-based catalysts. The optimized carbon-supported core-shell catalyst consisting of a Ru core and ultrathin RuO2 shell (Ru@RuO2/C) enables excellent ammonia Faradaic efficiency of over 90.0% from 0.05 to −0.2 V vs. RHE, with a maximum Faradaic efficiency of 99.91% and a yield rate of 2.18 mg h−1 mgcat −1 at 0 V vs. RHE. In situ spectroscopic analyses and theoretical calculations reveal that the Ru@RuO2/C effectively optimizes the adsorption of *NO3 and suppresses the HER owing to interfacial charge transfer and electron density redistribution across the Ru and RuO2 interface. Applying the Ru@RuO2/C as the cathode catalyst, the assembled Zinc−nitrate battery exhibits a peak power density of 60.5 mW cm−2 and a specific capacity of 829 mAh g−1 at 100 mA cm−2.
nb5fbeca26a68: Secure information transmission faces mounting challenges amid increasingly complex data processing and intrinsic physical limitations of conventional electronic systems. Multifunctional optoelectronic information platforms offer a promising route to overcome these constraints. Herein, we report a broad‐spectrum multifunctional optoelectronic transistor based on a type‐II organic p‐n heterojunction comprising p‐type C10‐DNTT and n‐type indandione‐terminated quinoidal compound Q4T‐4F. The extended π‐conjugation and quinoidal skeleton of Q4T‐4F significantly broaden its absorption spectrum, enabling the integration of broad‐spectrum photodetection, electrical synaptic emulation, and non‐volatile memory in a single device. The p‐n heterojunction transistor exhibits a broad spectral response from 300 to 1100 nm with a reconfigurable photoresponse modulated by both gate voltage and light intensity. Interface charge trapping endows the device with essential synaptic characteristics and robust multilevel non‐volatile memory performance. Leveraging these integrated functions, we demonstrate advanced applications including optical/electrical encryption‐decryption and reconfigurable logic gates. This work establishes a versatile platform for advancing optoelectronic systems toward secure and efficient information processing.
n3d09322c1262: Understanding the microscopic mechanisms governing charge transport in electronically doped conjugated polymers is important from both fundamental and device perspectives. Here, we investigate an amorphous semiconducting polymer, PTB7‐Th, as a suitable host to incorporate a specific organic salt system. The electronically disordered polymer, when doped with a split functional dopant that consists of organic cation 4‐(acetylamino)‐2,2,6,6‐tetramethyl‐1‐oxo‐piperidinium (ATOP) and the bulky anion tetrakis[3,5‐bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl] borate (BARF), undergoes a major enhancement in electrical transport. In addition to enhancing solubility, the BARF counterion effectively minimizes the coulombic interaction between the anion and the charge carrier on the polymer backbone, which facilitates efficient ion‐pair dissociation. A six‐order‐of‐magnitude enhancement in conductivity and a significant improvement in carrier mobility are observed in optimally doped samples. Temperature‐dependent DC conductivity measurements indicate variable‐range hopping transport, with improved hopping parameters upon doping. Additionally, AC measurements reveal faster carrier relaxation, systematic activation energy changes, and minimal ionic migration, highlighting improved electronic transport upon doping. Complementary molecular dynamics simulations capture ion–polaron and ion–ion correlations that rationalize the observed transport enhancement. The results highlight the connection from microscopic interactions to macroscopic enhancement in electrical performances while also identifying the origin of saturation beyond a critical dopant concentration.
n99ad21b436a5: Severe sodium polysulfides (NaPSs) shuttling and sluggish reaction kinetics substantially hinder the development of room‐temperature sodium‐sulfur (RT/Na‐S) batteries. Herein, a biomimetic uio‐66‐NH2‐assisted polyimide with carbon‐nanotube (uio@PI/CNT) for separator‐modification is proposed. Selective‐sieving effects induced via the inherent PI‐pore segmentation by uio‐66‐NH2 efficiently inhibit NaPSs shuttling and maintain a uniform Na+ flux for homogeneous Na‐deposition. Particularly, imide‐carbonyl and triazine moieties in PI, regarded as “electron sponge” capable of successive electron uptake and supply, exert the directional electron‐traction between external circuit and NaPSs to enable prompt electron‐donation to and electron‐extraction from NaPSs during discharging and charging, thereby remarkably reducing the sulfur‐conversion energy barriers. Integrating with enhanced electron‐conduction via CNT, effective binding with NaPSs, and high‐speed Na+ transport mediated via sufficient groups synergistically provided by PI and uio‐66‐NH2 for retaining active‐specie and timely replenishing reactants to PI catalytic centers, the fast reaction kinetics and highly stable anode are achieved. Consequently, a high reversible capacity (1248 mAh g−1) at 1 A g−1 with 96.7% cycling‐retention and an ultralow fading (0.0055%) per cycle even at 2 A g−1 are presented. The catalytic mechanism involving “electron sponge”, with the selective‐sieving effects, imparts a novel direction for exploiting the ultra‐durable sodium‐sulfur batteries.
ne8e8efaf5c47: Optical edge detection is emerging as a key technique in image processing owing to its merits of large-scale and real-time operation. However, achieving both broadband and high-contrast functionality remains challenging. While broadband optical edge detection has been demonstrated using nanograting-based geometric phase (GP) gratings, the relatively low image contrast limits their effectiveness. Here, we demonstrate high-efficiency nanopore-based GP gratings by ultrafast laser writing in silica glass, enabling high-contrast and broadband edge detection. A maximum contrast of 0.97 is achieved at 515 nm, approaching the theoretical limit of unity. We further show that the edge detection contrast and spatial resolution are influenced by the period of the GP gratings. Moreover, the nanopore-based GP gratings exhibit broadband performance from 450 to 2000 nm and support both one-dimensional and two-dimensional edge detection. Finally, we demonstrate edge detection capability in complex environments, e.g., through water or silicon at appropriate wavelengths.
na68cb191010b: Chiral gem-silylboronates represent a class of pivotal gem-dimetallic reagents in organic chemistry. Despite various synthetic methods emerged recently, the structural diversity of gem-silylboronates remains largely confined to alkyl-, (hetero)aryl-, and alkenyl-substituted variants; notably, alkynyl-substituted counterparts have remained largely underexplored. Herein, we report a Cu(I)/chiral bisoxazoline-catalyzed asymmetric insertion of α-alkynyl silyl carbenes into B–H bonds, affording a series of propargyl chiral gem-silylboronates and thus expanding the repertoire of organo-gem-dimetallics. This protocol features mild reaction conditions, broad functional group tolerance, and diverse downstream transformations, demonstrating significant synthetic utility. Furthermore, mechanistic experiments and theoretical calculations elucidate that the reaction proceeds via a concerted carbene insertion into the B–H bond, which likely serves as the rate-determining step. The enantioselectivity arises mainly from the shielding of the carbene Re face by the aryl groups on the oxazoline indenyl moiety, directing borane attack to the Si face, with additional enhancement from π–π interactions between the pyridine and indene rings. This work provides an efficient approach to chiral propargyl gem-silylboronates, further enriching the structural diversity and synthetic potential of chiral organosilicon–boron chemistry.
n185520bd85ff: Solar-driven conversion of N2 and H2O into ammonia under ambient conditions offers an alternative to the energy-intensive Haber–Bosch process, yet current advances are largely limited by material-focused strategies that insufficiently address coupled transport and interfacial reaction processes. Herein, we report a sub-nanofluidic photochemical membrane with catalytically active channels that integrate light harvesting, catalytic activation, and mass transport within a unified architecture for solar ammonia synthesis. The membrane consists of ZnIn2S4 atomically thin sheets and molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) quantum monolayers, forming ordered sub-nanometer channels that are intrinsically catalytic. This design establishes a confined reaction environment in which nanofluidic transport, gas–liquid interfacial regulation, and charge carrier dynamics are synergistically coupled. In particular, the combination of hydrophilic–hydrophobic interfaces and sub-nanofluidic-engineered serpentine flow pathways enhances reactant accessibility, residence time, and photon utilization, thereby overcoming diffusion and activation limitations typical of conventional photocatalytic systems. With these merits, the membrane achieves an ammonia production rate of 4.39 μg cm–2 h–1 (2.48 mmol gcat.–1 h–1) with ∼70% ammonia selectivity and maintains stable operation over 48 h of continuous testing. The achieved ammonia production rate compares favorably with those of reported photocatalytic platforms and some electrocatalytic N2 fixation systems. This work introduces a catalytically active nanofluidic channel paradigm for solar-driven N2 fixation and highlights the importance of material-transport co-engineering in bridging the gap between nanoscale catalytic design and device-level performance for chemical synthesis.
n6e770b5383b9: NiFe-based catalysts are highly active for the oxygen evolution reaction, but their precise fabrication on photoanodes at subnanometer scale for accelerating charge transport and maximizing active sites remains a challenge. Herein, we report a facile approach to deposit trimesic acid (TA) coordinated subnanometer Ni@Fe hydroxides (Ni-TA-Fe) on nanoporous WO3 photoanodes. This WO3/Ni-TA-Fe photoanode exhibited a record photocurrent density of ∼2.4 mA cm–2 at 1.23 VRHE under AM 1.5 G irradiation (100 mW cm–2) with an enhanced stability, which is much higher than that of pristine WO3 photoanodes. Comparative experiments, characterizations, and density functional theory calculations revealed that the subnanometer Ni catalyst layers could effectively inhibit the dissolution of W atoms from the surface lattice and promote the structural stability of the WO3 photoanode during PEC water oxidation. Furthermore, the strong coordination and electron-trapping capability of TA could efficiently promote charge redistribution in Fe catalyst layers, resulting in the activation and transformation of surface Fe sites into high-valence Fe4+ species for significantly improving the OER activity. This work provides the viable pathway to active and durable bimetallic catalysts to achieve high-performance and stable PEC water splitting.
n8f7cf49f1fe6: Understanding ion transport in the limit of infinite dilution is necessary for predicting the performance of electrochemical devices. While transport properties like ionic conductivity and diffusion coefficient can be readily extrapolated to zero concentration, establishing a reliable approach for determining the cation transference number with respect to the solvent velocity, t+0, remains a challenge. To address this challenge, we introduce an approach based on Newman's concentrated solution theory and fundamental dilute-limit constraints. We validate the approach using experimental data for a poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO)/ sodium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (NaTFSI) electrolyte and derive a simple quadratic equation relating t+0 to readily measurable transport properties. Our approach has the potential to provide more accurate models of concentration gradients and limiting current in electrochemical systems, thereby improving their use in design and optimization.
nb4e49d194ace: Existing alloy anodes suffer from high redox potentials and sluggish Li atomic kinetics, limiting the energy density and rate capability of all-solid-state lithium batteries (ASSLBs). Herein, we report a well-designed Li3Ga2 alloy anode that simultaneously delivers an ultralow Li deposition potential (0.007 V vs. Li+/Li) and fast Li atomic diffusion kinetics (2.0 × 10–8 cm2 s–1). The high Li atomic diffusivity primarily originates from moderate Li/Ga antisite mixing, stabilizing the anode-solid electrolyte interface and enabling a high critical current density of 24 mA cm–2 in ASSLBs. Coupled with a LiCoO2 cathode, the ASSLB delivers a high initial Coulombic efficiency of 96.5% and an ultralong cycle life of 2000 cycles at room temperature, with a high output voltage of 3.84 V, outperforming state-of-the-art alloy-based counterparts. A practical all-solid-state pouch cell employing the LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 cathode also delivers outstanding cycling stability. This work redefines alloy anode design principles through synergistic optimization of Li deposition potential and Li atomic diffusivity.
n090dd465462c: Organic semiconductor molecules are key elements for the development of next-generation flexible and lightweight electronic devices. Their performance is largely governed by molecular arrangement within thin films, whereas environmental sensing is governed by surface functionality and mediated by the interfacial structure at the solid–gas interface. However, experimental tools capable of accessing such information with molecular-scale resolution remain scarce. Here, we employ third-eigenmode atomic force microscopy (AFM) with moderately compliant cantilevers to directly probe the interfacial solvation structure of the liquid layer formed at the interface between small-molecule organic semiconductor thin films and the ambient gas environment. This approach also enables true molecular-resolution imaging across molecular steps, providing detailed insight into interplanar molecular organization and crystal growth mechanisms. Overall, our results establish third-eigenmode AFM as a versatile methodology for high-resolution characterization of molecular packing and for elucidating the relationship between surface functionality and interfacial structure in organic semiconductor materials.
n1a90b504e378: For pharmacological treatments of brain disorders, the blood–brain barrier (BBB) poses a formidable obstacle, tightly restricting the cerebral uptake of therapeutic agents. Tight junction (TJ) binders, including peptides, proteins, and monoclonal antibodies, that specifically bind to the extracellular domains (ECDs) of TJ proteins are increasingly being explored as BBB-weakening agents for enhanced drug delivery to the brain. Given that nanobodies (Nbs) can access epitopes that are often inaccessible to conventional antibodies, we obtained 16 Nbs with unique CDRs via immunization of alpaca with the ECD of either human (h) or murine JAM-1 (mJAM-1), a major TJ protein. Twelve Nb candidates exhibited high-affinity binding to mJAM-1, as measured by surface plasmon resonance (SPR), and these interactions were further validated for 9 Nbs by immunostaining of JAM-1-overexpressing cells. Five Nbs were found to weaken the barrier of the eGFP-hCldn5-MDCKII cellular monolayer, as shown by reduced transendothelial electrical resistance (TEER). X-ray crystallography revealed that the lead barrier-weakening Nb, E6, binds to the membrane-proximal nondimeric D2 domain of mJAM-1. Mutating key residues at this interface eliminated the BBB-weakening effect of E6, as evidenced by unaltered sodium fluorescence (NaFI) leakage in both eGFP-hCldn5-MDCKII and mJAM1-mGL-MDCKII cellular monolayers compared with the nontreated control. Our study highlights the potential of JAM-1-targeting Nbs as BBB modulators, offering a promising approach for generating TJ binders to enhance brain drug delivery.
neae1789f5ca7: Surface texturing in crystalline silicon solar cells imposes a fundamental trade‐off in perovskite‐silicon tandems: micrometer‐scale pyramids enable efficient light trapping but limit the conformal deposition of thin perovskite films with sub‐micrometer thickness, whereas reduced texture heights improve compatibility at the expense of optical performance and interfacial quality of the tandem device. Here, we address this challenge by combining precisely controlled submicron texturing with an ozone‐assisted chemical rounding treatment. The resulting silicon substrates feature smoothly rounded, symmetric submicron textures that suppress micro‐terrace formation and partial epitaxy at the amorphous silicon/crystalline silicon interface, while promoting more spatially uniform optoelectronic properties in the subsequently integrated top‐cell stack. The morphology‐engineered texture yields a monolithic perovskite–silicon tandem device with a power conversion efficiency of 33.25%, demonstrating that multiscale morphological control provides a powerful pathway to simultaneously improve the optical performance and interfacial quality of tandem solar cells.
n3e536cdda65a: Disordered rocksalt cathodes (DRX) represent a compelling platform for cobalt- and nickel-free high-energy density lithium-ion batteries. Yet their scalable synthesis remains challenging, especially for metastable DRX chemistries that have been predominantly developed via mechanochemical routes. A prominent example is polyanion-integrated DRX (DRXPS) cathodes, which rank among the best DRX cathodes reported to date in terms of reversible energy density, but have thus far been synthesized only mechanochemically via low-temperature ball milling. Here we demonstrate a coprecipitation–enabled solid-state synthesis of a DRXPS cathode, Li1.67Mn1.5P0.17O4, translating a mechanochemical route into a scalable process that is compatible with established cathode manufacturing infrastructure. The workflow programs precursor chemistry via coprecipitation of Mn2 + with HPO4 2 − and OH−, followed by a eutectic lithium-salt-assisted solid-state reaction, enabling low-thermal-budget DRXPS formation (450°C, 30 min) in air. The reduced thermal budget suppresses particle coarsening and yields a mixed micro-/nanoscale particle morphology, thereby eliminating the need for post-synthesis particle pulverization. The resulting cathodes deliver 324 mAh g−1 (935 Wh kg−1), demonstrating that high-energy density DRXPS can be realized within a manufacturing-compatible workflow. This work establishes a direct pathway toward scalable production of metastable high-energy density DRXPS cathodes and identifies precursor engineering as the key enabler.
n8badefa6f072: Photoelectrochemical water oxidation is limited not simply by light absorption, but by inefficient hole routing and utilization at the semiconductor‐electrolyte interface, together with severe defect‐mediated recombination. Here, a self‐reconstructed crystallinity‐differentiated interface is developed to program hole utilization in photoanodes. A one‐step hydrothermal synthesis creates an interlocked architecture in which highly crystalline In2S3 pyramids are coupled with a disordered mixed‐anion nanosheet domain, generating a spatially polarized reaction field for directed hole accumulation and transfer. This reconstructed interface lowers the work function, redistributes the local coordination environment around In sites, and induces a spatially heterogeneous photovoltage landscape that promotes interfacial charge separation. Mild Ar annealing further serves as a defect‐selective activation step, suppressing recombination‐active defects while preserving the beneficial interfacial polarization, thereby accelerating charge injection and oxygen evolution kinetics. The optimized photoanode reaches 8.74 mA cm−2 at 1.23 VRHE, establishing interlocked crystallinity‐differentiated architecture engineering combined with defect‐selective activation as an effective strategy for sulfide photoanodes.
n0cb25c6982f1: Protein-based biological nanopores have emerged as versatile tools for sequencing biopolymers, identifying molecules, and probing reactions at the single-molecule level. Many biological nanopores have been characterized, revealing the significance of nanopore size, shape, and chemical composition in molecular detection and discrimination. Advancements in understanding the nanofluidic properties of nanopores have complemented engineering approaches expanding the possible applications of nanopore technology. Through a combination of structural insights, rational design, systematic screening, and molecular dynamics simulations, researchers have developed nanopores capable of distinguishing between ions, nucleic acids, peptides, and folded proteins with remarkable specificity and sensitivity. Building upon three decades of progress, this Review highlights recent engineering innovations, discusses ongoing challenges, and explores the prospects in the field.
n86c10ac47798: Rearrangement reactions are critical transformations in organic synthesis, and a comprehensive look at how they have been utilized so far in polymeric contexts is missing. Historically, these transformations have been implemented within the polymer periphery (e.g., side chains), and recently, there has been an expanding effort to implement them into polymer backbones. Considering these efforts, we compile the history of rearrangement reactions as applied in polymer contexts, detailing mechanisms, reaction conditions, goals for implementation of rearrangement, and location of implementation (i.e., propagating species, side chains, polymer backbones). In organizing this work, we hope to guide the further development of rearrangements as general tools for polymer modification and design.
